source.title: MALTO at SemEval-2025 Task 4: Dual Teachers for Unlearning Sensitive Content in LLMs
source.authors: Claudio Savelli; E. A. Munis; E. Bayat; A. Grieco; F. Giobergia

record.tranche_reason: Evaluates unlearning methods with regurgitation and capability measures, but does not test the recovery attacks at the center of the broader claim.
record.gate_note: The paper measures forgetting, retained-set regurgitation, MMLU utility, and membership-inference performance. Membership inference is not a test of recovering the forgotten knowledge. It does not test fine-tuning recovery, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompt-only recovery. The aggregate score does not isolate a claim version.
record.test_reason: In a new setting (SemEval-2025 LUME, OLMo-1B), the study measures forget-set regurgitation and utility for several unlearning methods. That bears on the first two parts of version A. It runs no recovery attack, so B–F and A's 'simple attacks don't recover it' part are untested. Membership inference is a distinguishability test, not knowledge recovery.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say dual-teacher unlearning forgets the forget set, keeps MMLU, beats the baselines on aggregate score and MIA, but loses retain-set information (a trade-off). They also infer from MIA .984 that the knowledge was 'entirely erased'. That inference is not tested by any recovery attack, and the 'kept MMLU' claim is uninformative because OLMo-1B scores near chance on MMLU.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes a dual-teacher distillation method adapted from Bad Teaching, and compares it with Gradient Ascent and other baselines; it does not reproduce the recovery-attack recipes in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Ordered versus non-ordered training and choice of Incompetent Teacher change the reported scores; the authors say non-ordered training generally performs better.

fits_no_version.finding: MIA scores after unlearning: DT (R-U) .984, GA .885, GD .000, KL div .001. The authors read high scores as forgotten samples being indistinguishable from unseen ones.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dual-teacher and gradient-ascent unlearning reduce membership-inference distinguishability of forgotten samples.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 19th International Workshop on Semantic Evaluation (SemEval-2025), ACL
record.problems: Only OLMo-1B was evaluated because of hardware limitations. The paper reports aggregate task scores without uncertainty estimates. The qualitative example is limited to a displayed sample; the paper does not evaluate the recovery attacks in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: The Total Aggregation Score was omitted because it combines multiple metrics and does not isolate a claim version. Other prose about output divergence is not a direct measure of recovery or general ability.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks (fine-tuning, prompting, quantization, probing) recover the forgotten data. Utility on a general benchmark the 1B model performs above chance on.
No activation ablation or access-versus-deletion analysis.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, cross-lingual or in-context recovery.

record.verdict_notes: Table 2 column misread for GD RRf (.063, not .885). r17-r23 duplicate r33-r39. Table 3 is a KL heat map of fixed text, not a generation, so the reader's 'challenges' label from r40-r41 is unfounded. The paper is a SemEval workshop entry with a single 1B model and no uncertainty.

versions.untested_parts: The paper evaluates forget-set performance and MMLU utility, but does not test whether simple recovery attacks can restore the knowledge.
No post-unlearning recovery by fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten examples.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of access-blocking versus deletion.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, other-language, or in-context recovery tests.
The paper does not test whether a method resists the recovery attacks listed in the claim.

relationships.condition: Dual-teacher variants and Gradient Ascent on OLMo-1B
relationships.reason: Forget-set RRf reaches .93–.999 (r02-r06), but retain-set RRr collapses from .991 to .000–.06 (r33-r37); forgetting comes with loss of retained knowledge.
relationships.display_finding: Forget RRf reached 0.93–0.999, while retain RRr collapsed from 0.991 to 0.000–0.06.

relationships.reason: GD leaves the forget set almost intact (RRf .063 vs .007 Original) while keeping retain ability (.924) (r07, r38).
relationships.display_finding: Forget-set RRf remained 0.063 versus original 0.007, while retain ability stayed at 0.924.

relationships.reason: Forgetting is partial (RRf .560) and retain ability is partly lost (.467) (r08, r39).
relationships.display_finding: KL minimization produced partial forgetting with RRf 0.560 and reduced retained ability with RRr 0.467.
